Both arms are measured in the identical regime, so the comparison is sound. Scored with EOS decisions visible (`ignore_eos` instrument, rig `d3a81119`) on the BF16 trajectory recorded 2026-10-07; a byte-identical 8-bit bridge re-run showed the environment unchanged. At all 25 BF16 end-of-sequence positions in tokens 1-64 (38 of 38 over 256 tokens) the 4-bit pack also picks `</s>`, and it never picks `</s>` anywhere else, so end-of-sequence decisions are not a source of the drift. One 256-token run (2026-10-07) authored this card from its first 64 tokens per prompt, a scope fixed before the run; its overall figure gives the same verdict: top-1 91.50% (Wilson [91.20%, 91.80%], 33111 positions). 4 of 160 prompts were skipped because the server tokenized a forced trajectory prefix differently than the BF16 trajectory implied (1 code explanation, 1 factual recall, 2 instruction-following), so those positions are unmeasured; even if all 256 of their first-64-token positions had been agreements, the 64-token Wilson upper bound would be 92.65%, far below 99%.
